title: One-Pot Chicken, Broccoli & Cheddar Rice
description: Ground chicken, rice, broccoli, and cheddar cook into a simple cozy one-pot dinner with familiar ingredients.
equipment: large deep skillet or Dutch oven with lid
substitutions: Use ground turkey instead of chicken.
Use frozen broccoli florets; add them straight from frozen and allow an extra minute or two.
Use Monterey Jack instead of cheddar.

cookSteps.text: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add 1 pound ground chicken or turkey and cook 5–6 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until no pink remains.
Stir in 1 cup white rice, 2 cups chicken broth, and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. Bring to a simmer, cover, reduce heat to low, and cook 15 minutes.
Scatter 2 cups small broccoli florets over the rice. Cover again and cook 4–5 minutes, until the rice and broccoli are tender.
Remove from the heat. Stir in 1 cup shredded cheddar until melted. Rest 2 minutes, then serve.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days. Reheat with a spoonful of water or broth until steaming hot.

title: Turkey, Cheddar & Cucumber Ranch Wraps
description: Crunchy cucumber, deli turkey, cheddar, and a little ranch make a fast cold lunch with no cooking required.
substitutions: Use mayonnaise plus a pinch of garlic powder instead of ranch.

cookSteps.text: Lay out 2 large tortillas. Spread each with 1 tablespoon ranch dressing.
Divide 6 ounces deli turkey, 1/2 cup shredded cheddar, 1/2 sliced cucumber, and up to 1 cup shredded lettuce between the tortillas.
Fold in the sides, roll each tortilla tightly, cut in half if you like, and serve.

storage: Best assembled just before eating. Prepared wraps can be refrigerated up to 1 day, though the cucumber will soften the tortilla.

title: Leftover Roast Beef & Noodle Skillet
description: Cooked roast beef, noodles, peas, and a quick creamy sauce become a warm leftover-rescue dinner in about 15 minutes.
substitutions: Use leftover cooked steak or pot roast instead of roast beef.
Use frozen mixed vegetables instead of peas.
Use cooked rotini or macaroni instead of egg noodles.

cookSteps.text: Whisk 1/2 cup milk with 1 tablespoon cornstarch until smooth. Pour it into a large skillet with 1 cup beef broth and 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder if using.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring, and cook about 2 minutes until lightly thickened.
Stir in 3 cups cooked noodles, 1 1/2 cups chopped cooked roast beef, and 1 cup frozen peas. Cook 6–7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything is steaming hot and the peas are tender.
Taste, season with salt and pepper if needed, and serve.

storage: Make this only while the original beef and noodles are still within their safe refrigerated storage window. Refrigerate skillet leftovers up to 2 days and reheat until steaming hot.

title: Small-Batch Caramel Apple Oat Cookie Cups
description: Six soft oat cookie cups hold a quick brown-sugar apple filling for a small, cozy dessert without specialty ingredients.
substitutions: Use a firm pear instead of apple.
Use quick oats instead of old-fashioned oats.
Add a pinch of nutmeg if you already have it.

steps.text: Mix and shape the oat cups.

cookSteps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease 6 muffin cups. Mix 4 tablespoons softened butter with 1/4 cup brown sugar. Stir in 1/2 cup flour, 1/2 cup oats, and 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon until crumbly but able to hold together when pressed.
Divide the oat mixture among 6 muffin cups. Press it firmly across each bottom and a little way up the sides to make shallow cups.
Mix 1 finely diced small apple with 1 tablespoon brown sugar and 1 tablespoon water. Spoon the apples into the oat cups.
Bake 17–18 minutes, until the oat edges are golden and the apples are tender.
Cool in the pan 10 minutes before loosening the cookie cups with a butter knife.

storage: Store covered in the refrigerator up to 3 days. Warm briefly before serving if you like.
